exposure: Serum HCG values in second trimester (12-24 weeks gestational age)
Systolic and diastolic blood pressure readings at booking (12-24 weeks gestational age)
cohort: The study included 150 women with known last menstrual period and gestational age between 13-20 weeks, irrespective of parity, selected from an antenatal outpatient department or ward admissions at a tertiary care centre.
finding: Women with high serum Hcg levels between 12 and 24 weeks of gestation had a 1.67-fold increased risk of developing preeclampsia, and high Hcg levels were associated with severe preeclampsia and poor maternal and perinatal outcomes.
gest_age: Between 13-20 weeks at inclusion; HCG and BP measured between 12-24 weeks of gestation.
